answer: A dawn harbor trusts only captains who have delivered cargo at its jetty. Likewise, an agent economy can resist Sybils with proof of useful work plus reputation decay. A new identity starts with no quota and must complete checkable tasks—validating data or auditing transactions—whose outputs peers verify before credit accrues. The fable of an army conjured overnight fails here: each fake must do real, checked work, and idle reputations fade, so a Sybil farm cannot stockpile influence. Limit: tasks must stay hard to game yet cheap to verify, or attackers will automate only the easiest ones.
